source.title: Source and scope.
source.text: The calculation follows CLT article 64 for monthly employees: monthly salary divided by 30 times daily duration, with weekly hours converted by weekly hours / 6 x 30.
source.disclaimer: Gross estimate tool only, with no legal, labor, tax, or accounting advice.

howToCalculate.title: How to calculate hourly salary in Brazil
howToCalculate.p1: For monthly employees, divide monthly gross salary by the applicable monthly divisor. With R$3,000.00 and divisor 220, the normal gross hourly value is R$13.64.
howToCalculate.p2: The divisor should reflect the schedule or payroll criterion. The calculator shows the math so you can compare it with contract, payslip, or collective agreement.

divisor220.title: Why 44 weekly hours commonly become divisor 220
divisor220.p1: CLT article 64 uses 30 times daily duration. In the 44-hour weekly convention distributed across 6 days, the daily average is 7.3333 hours.
divisor220.p2: Multiplying 44 / 6 x 30 gives a monthly divisor of 220 hours. The same logic turns 40 weekly hours into divisor 200.

alternateDivisors.title: How to use divisor 200, 180, 150, or manual
alternateDivisors.text: Enter weekly hours to derive the divisor, or choose manual divisor when the contract, professional category, collective agreement, 12x36 schedule, or payroll policy uses another number.

hourlyToMonthly.title: How to estimate monthly salary from hourly value
hourlyToMonthly.text: In hourly-to-monthly mode, the tool multiplies gross hourly value by the divisor. This helps compare an hourly proposal with a gross monthly base.

notIncluded.title: What the calculator does not calculate
notIncluded.p1: It does not calculate net salary, INSS, IRRF, FGTS, DSR, official overtime, night-shift additional, time bank, benefits, absences, commissions, or payslip.
notIncluded.p2: Use net salary, INSS, FGTS, or severance calculators for those bases. This page stays limited to gross hourly conversion.

q1.question: How do I calculate my hourly salary?
q1.answer: Divide monthly gross salary by the applicable monthly divisor. For a common 44-hour weekly schedule, the divisor often used is 220.

q2.question: What is divisor 220?
q2.answer: It is the common conversion from 44 weekly hours to monthly hours: 44 / 6 x 30 = 220.

q3.question: Does a 40-hour week use divisor 200?
q3.answer: By the same convention, 40 weekly hours produce divisor 200. Still, contract and payroll rules may prevail.

q4.question: Can I use a manual divisor?
q4.answer: Yes. Use manual divisor when the payslip, contract, collective agreement, or professional category indicates another divisor.

q5.question: Does the calculator show net salary?
q5.answer: No. It is gross-only and does not calculate INSS, IRRF, FGTS, or benefits. Use the net salary calculator for that.

q6.question: Is the 50% additional amount official overtime?
q6.answer: No. It is only a simple gross multiplier. Official overtime may require DSR, night-shift rules, time bank, taxes, and payroll rules.

q7.question: Do 12x36, bank workers, teachers, or special categories use the same math?
q7.answer: Not always. Categories, shifts, and agreements can have their own divisor or treatment, so manual mode and professional review matter.

q8.question: Why might my payslip use another divisor?
q8.answer: Payroll may follow contract, collective agreement, category, employer setup, court decision, or a specific rule this estimate cannot know.
